request.state: The sample mean converges toward the expectation as the number of independent observations grows. That convergence, known as the law of large numbers, sustains much of the modern statistical inference and the analysis of experimental data. Estimators are compared by their bias and variance. Hypothesis tests control the probability of false discoveries. Regression models describe how variables change together. Random sampling reduces the risk of systematic distortions. Sample sizes matter very much. Outliers distort the mean more than the median. Good designs reduce bias and variance at once.
